messages:
Aisha: Hey team, quick bring-up note for Sprout-10B (new upstream). Did a short quant sweep (fp16 / int8 / int6) and have some econ vs quality numbers.
Ben: Nice — any red flags?
Aisha: int6 looks promising on throughput but we observed summarization truncation on long docs. Sample metric: ROUGE-L drop ~6 points vs fp16 on longform >1024 tokens.
Carol: Do you have latency/cost numbers?
Aisha: Yes. p95 latency (short chat): fp16 320ms, int8 210ms, int6 170ms. Token cost per 1k (normalized): fp16 $1.00, int8 $0.62, int6 $0.48.
Dmitri: So int6 saves ~52% vs fp16 but has quality hit on longform. What about instruction-following and safety signals?
Aisha: Instruction pass-rate (binary eval on our 500 prompt set): fp16 94%, int8 92%, int6 88%. Safety filter false positive rate unchanged. Int6 regression concentrated on multi-step summarization and some code-generation edge cases.
Elaine: For GTN/product, what's the suggested routing? Mixed fleet?
Ben: Proposed quick playbook:
- Canary: route 5% of traffic to int6 for chat-style, high-SLA low-cost flows
- Shadow/eval: collect 100k samples from longform routes and run offline ROUGE/EM checks
- Fallback: if summary-length > 1024 or prompt contains "multi-step", force int8 or fp16
Carol: Do we have a simple rule to infer "longform" cheaply (without tokenizing fully)?
Dmitri: Use heuristics: input char count > 6k or contains newlines > 8 -> treat as longform. Good enough for routing.
Aisha: Also added a quick scorecard we can use for canary gates:
- QoQ delta ROUGE-L (longform) <= 2 pts
- Instruction pass-rate delta <= 1.5%
- p95 latency budget <= 220ms for chat flows
- Unit cost reduction >= 40% to justify int6 use
Ben: That seems reasonable. What about monitoring thresholds and automation?
Aisha: I sketched an alert set:
- metric: rolling 24h ROUGE-L delta on sampled longform > 3 -> auto rollback of int6 to int8
- metric: instruction pass-rate drop > 2% over 12h -> notify ML-oncall
- metric: p99 latency spike +30% -> throttle int6 batch size
Carol: Any config snippets for routing / rollout we want in the console? I can add to the rollout template.
Aisha: Draft config:
```
route_rules:
  - name: sprout-int6-chat
    match: "channel == 'chat' and char_count < 6000"
    percent: 5
    model_variant: sprout-10b-int6
    fallback: sprout-10b-int8
  - name: sprout-longform
    match: "char_count >= 6000 or newlines > 8"
    percent: 100
    model_variant: sprout-10b-int8
```
Elaine: For product /GTN messaging: propose we recommend int8 as the default for now and int6 as an opt-in cost tier for high-throughput non-longform. That keeps user experience conservative.
Dmitri: Agree. Also recommend a small priming test for caching effects — many of these longform regressions shrink when we enable prefix KV cache and 2-step warmstart.
Aisha: Good call. I ran a quick warmstart experiment: enabling warmstart reduced ROUGE-L delta on int6 from 6 -> 3.5 pts for long docs, and p95 improved by ~15ms.
Ben: Sounds like a hybrid approach then: int6 for chat + cached/warmstart; int8 for longform. Make sure billing labels show unit cost delta so customers see savings.
Carol: I'll add the scorecard and the rollout rules to the canary template. Any specific slices to monitor?
Aisha: Yes: multi-turn summarization, code-gen (>= 40 lines), and bullet-point extraction. Tag requests with `slice:sprout_longform` and `slice:sprout_code` so we can compute per-slice deltas.
Elaine: What's the immediate ask from Product/GTN for docs?
Aisha: 1) Guidance: default int8, opt-in int6 for chat with clear caveats; 2) Short TL;DR on expected savings and latency numbers; 3) Example rollout json + monitoring dashboard link.
Ben: I'll draft the GTN blurb: "Sprout-10B — int8 recommended for parity, int6 optional for cost-conscious conversational flows. Expect ~40-50% savings; some quality regressions on longform summarization may occur." :memo:
eval-bot: Automated sample check complete. 5k random chat samples -> human pass-rate simulated 91% on int6 vs 93% on int8.
Dmitri: Thanks @Aisha. Next steps: Aisha to push canary config, Carol to add dashboard, Ben to write GTN blurb. Revisit after 48h of canary data.
Elaine: +1. I'll loop in Solutions for any immediate customer asks.
Aisha: Pushing canary now, will post updates. :rocket:
